residual_risk: THE BYTE-IDENTITY CHECK WAS NOT RUN. `node bin/hkb.js dispatch --dry-run --json` was refused by this worker session's launch guard — a worker may not run dispatch, by design, since a second dispatcher double-claims. Disclosed rather than routed around. What stands in its place: test/dispatch.test.js exercises tick() against the fake-gh double and passes unchanged, and every function the dry run reaches was moved rather than rewritten. A reviewer should still run the comparison on kb/track-288 and on this branch before merging.

branchFallbackPrs is not in the card's §3 list of what moves to forge.js, but went there with openPrsByHead: it is pure PR logic and src/tasks.js had to become a shim, so it could not stay. src/store/github.js imports it back for fillPrFallback. test/tasks.test.js still imports it from src/tasks.js and passes.

The interface's createTask/updateBody/claim signatures differ from the legacy functions they call (§6.4 shapes vs today's). Both are exported; a caller that mixes them up gets a silent wrong-argument bug rather than a throw. Only the conformance suite uses the interface methods today.

The GitHub store's board()/setBoard() read and write .kanban/board.json via loadBoard/saveBoard at storeRoot(ctx). That is a reasonable reading of §6.4 for a driver whose board has no document of its own, but it is a choice this card made, not one the plan states — the local drivers will read the board.json ON the kb-board branch instead, and the two must not be assumed interchangeable.

listLocks() returns beat_at: null for every row on the GitHub driver — the ref listing carries no commit date, and filling it would be one request per lock. Callers that need it call lockBeatAt(n, k). A local driver will populate it, so a caller written against the local shape would silently see nulls on GitHub.

results.summary:
Board state now sits behind one interface. `openStore(ctx)` (src/store/index.js) carries the §6.4 method names of docs/local-first.md as the contract A4/A5 implement in parallel, plus STORE_METHODS for the conformance suite to check a driver's shape against. src/store/github.js is src/tasks.js + src/lock.js moved VERBATIM with one wrapper at the bottom exposing them under those names; capabilities() returns {events:false} and events() refuses with exit 2 rather than answering an empty list. The per-tick comments memo and its invalidation are byte-for-byte unchanged. src/forge.js holds the pull-request half — openPrsByHead, branchFallbackPrs, prMergeStates, enableAutoMerge, branchProtection, mergePullRequest, prChecksState from tasks.js plus prNodeId/isGithubUser/finishPr from lifecycle.js — and also re-exports GhError/isOffline so lifecycle.js (outbox) and dispatch.js (reclaim clock), which only classify a transport failure, stop importing gh.js. src/tasks.js and src/lock.js are now re-export shims, which is why no caller changed beyond import lines and no existing test was edited. storeRoot(ctx) in src/board.js is the common git dir's parent via mainWorktree, never --show-toplevel. test/store.test.js is the driver-parametrised conformance suite: one SCENARIOS array, a DRIVERS list holding the GitHub driver over test/fake-gh.js in a real git repo with a real remote.

FOR THE NEXT NODE: the interface method names are frozen — adding one means adding a scenario. createTask({title,body,kb,status,agent}) and updateBody(n, body) take §6.4's signatures, NOT today's createIssue/updateBody argument shapes; the legacy functions are exported unchanged beside them, and new verbs should use the interface. store.claim() returns {result, token} where token is the GitHub driver's sha (ref/error ride along). A local driver appends to DRIVERS and gets the three optional harness hooks — settleClaim, reclaim, recordBeat — for what the interface cannot express; nothing else may reach a driver's internals or the scenario stops being portable. PR #309 targets kb/track-288, so Closes #291 will not auto-close; the track branch's own PR into main lands it.
